problem: Given that the expression $3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Phase for the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
examples.problem: Given that the expression $2\sin{x}-2\cos{x}$ can be written as $R\sin(x-\phi)$ with $0^\circ  <       \phi <        90^\circ$ and $R>0,$ what is the value of $\phi?$
examples.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2 \sin x - 2 \cos x = R\sin(x-\phi),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2 \sin x - 2 \cos x   = (R \cos \phi ) \sin x - (R \sin \phi ) \cos x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\sin x$ and $\cos x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
9\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
9\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=9 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={9}^{2}+{3}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =81+9 \\ {R}^{2} & =90 \\ R & =\sqrt{90} \\  & =3\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$
